info.timeAllocation: Study hour (150h) = 45 contact hours (60 sessions) + 1.25 hours final exam + 103.75 hours self-study
info.prerequisite: Passed LTG202 and ENG302c/ENG303 and ENP101/ENP102
info.description:
This course is designed to help introduce to the students the basics of Semantics in a step by step process through Semantics 101. In addition to the Semantics a Coursebook unit outlines, the course is enhanced with supplementary activities corresponding to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages. The course will help students:

- have a grasp of the basics of Semantics through class discussions and presentations

- discover the use of the basics of Semantics in oral and written communication by conducting collaborative discussions and using AI-assisted tools

- interact confidently with the lecturer and fellow students in dissolving disagreements about their answers during collaborative discussions

- engage in collaborative discussions with the lecturer and fellow students in preparing group presentations and a group project using appropriate language in oral and written communication skills.

- apply semantic theory and AI-assisted tools to investigate meaning phenomena in English language by conducting a group project

- understand and produce academic writing paper that demonstrates theoretical understanding, critical reasoning, and evidence-based argumentation

- develop professional communication and academic presentation skills through group presentations, oral project defense and collaborative discussions

- cultivate students’ awareness of ethical and responsible use of linguistic data, theories, and AI technology

Teaching and Learning Approaches /Pedagogical Approaches

- Direct Instruction

- Constructivist Approach

-Workshop-based Learning

- Inquiry-based Learning

- Case-based Learning

- Practice-based Learning

- Scaffolded Instruction

- Collaborative Learning

- Problem-based Learning

- Project-based Learning

- Digital Literacy Pedagogy

Assessment scheme:

On-going assessment >0, Final Exam Score >=4/10 & Final Result >=5/10

clos.loDetails: Define and explain the foundational concepts of semantics and recognise their relevance in meaning construction in a language
Demonstrate ethical behavior, intercultural awareness, collaboration, and reflective learning in exploring meaning, and presenting meaning in language
Analyse how referring expressions, predicates, deixis, definiteness, extensions and prototypes operate in English texts or discourse
Analyze sense relations and semantic phenomena in English language through structured examples, corpora, and AI-assisted tools
Use logical formulae and semantic tests to explain ambiguity, entailment, and paraphrase in English sentences
Integrate semantic knowledge with syntax, pragmatics, and discourse analysis to interpret meaning in communication
Conduct a small-scale semantic group project that investigates meaning in real-world communication
Use AI tools collaboratively and responsibly to support inquiry, visualization, and presentation of project outcomes
Produce a well-organized written paper in English to investigate semantic phenomena by integrating theory, data, and AI-supported analysis
Deliver an academic oral presentation and defense in English on semantic phenomena with demonstrated critical reasoning, communication, and professionalism
